name: Starter: Azerbaijani
about: Azerbaijani in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Azerbaijani order.

words.sən: you (to a friend; sənə: to you)
words.deyil: not (with a noun or describing word)
words.var: there is; with a possessed noun: have
words.bilmək: know; be able to (-a bilər: can)

zehmet-olmasa.about: Literally if it's no trouble; the same to anyone.

items.text: Bir çay və bir su, zəhmət olmasa.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Bir çaylar və bir su, zəhmət olmasa.
Bir çay və bir sular, zəhmət olmasa.

items.means: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
I live in a small house.
My mother goes to the city.
Tomorrow I go to the city.

items.text: Bir qardaşım və bir bacım var.
items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
wrong: Mən bir qardaş və bir bacı var.

items.means: The keys are on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.
My mom is making lunch in the kitchen.
We live in a small apartment.
The kids are playing in the park.

items.text: Mənə bir stəkan su verin, zəhmət olmasa.
items.means: Please give me a glass of water.
wrong: Mən bir stəkan su verin, zəhmət olmasa.

items.means: We had lunch at a restaurant yesterday.
I drink my coffee with milk.
I'm going to the store to buy bread.
I like fish, but I don't like meat.
wrong: Balığı sevirəm, amma əti sevirəm deyil.

items.means: We're going to the market tomorrow.
I go to work by bus.
The train is ten minutes late.
We went to Baku by train.
Does this bus go to the center?
I came home late from work.
What are you doing this weekend?
I have to get up early tomorrow.

concept.line: A verb's ending says who does it, so mən (I), sən (you) and biz (we) are often left out: içirəm (I drink), içirsən (you drink), içirik (we drink).
Is is the ending -dır or -dir (and its harmony forms), and I am is -am or -əm: Anam müəllimdir (my-mom teacher-is), Mən Amerikadanam (I from-America-am).

words.means: müəlliməm = I am a teacher; müəllimsən = you are a teacher; müəllim = teacher
anam = my mother; anamdır = is my mother
atam = my father; atamdır = is my father

concept.line: Whose something is is an ending: anam (my mom), adın (your name), evimiz (our house), uşaqlarınız (your children).

words.means: yoxdur = there is not; do not have

concept.line: -da or -də is in or at: evdə (at home), Bakıda (in Baku), soyuducuda (in the fridge).

words.means: danışırsan = you speak; danışıram = I speak
anlamıram = I do not understand; anlayırsan = you understand

concept.line: -ır, -ir, -ur or -ür marks what's happening now or usually, with a person ending where needed: işləyir (works), içirəm (I drink), oynayırlar (they play).

words.means: ev = house; evdə = in a house
yaşayıram = I live; yaşayırsan = you live; yaşayır = lives
gedirəm = I go; I am going; gedirsən = you go; you are going; gedir = goes; is going

concept.line: A question word stays where its answer would go, and a yes-or-no question can keep a statement's order with the voice rising: Adın nədir?

words.means: işləyirəm = I work; işləməliyəm = I have to work
bilmirəm = to know; as an auxiliary after a verb in -a/-ə: to be able to
getməliyəm = I have to go; gedə = go
